item.title: Formalisation of information processing and intelligence in proteinoid networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.13545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proteinoid microspheres are electrically active assemblies of thermally polymerised amino acids that exhibit spontaneous oscillations, spike-like events, stimulus-dependent responses, adaptation and collective dynamics. We formulate these observations as an applied-mathematical problem and develop a unified dynamical framework for information processing in proteinoid networks. Individual microspheres are represented by nonlinear excitable or oscillatory systems, whereas interactions are described by weighted adaptive graphs and, in the spatial limit, reaction--diffusion dynamics. The framework combines signal propagation, attenuation, fading memory, adaptive coupling, synchronisation, information transfer, reservoir readout, robustness and energetic constraints. We define a task-relative proteinoid intelligence functional from normalised measures of stimulus information, memory, adaptation, directed information transfer, task performance and robustness, penalised by energetic and structural costs. Analytical results establish a joint-response information bound, an upper bound on linear memory for stable linear networks, and existence of an optimal admissible coupling matrix under compact constraints. Dimensionless groups identify the relative time scales and coupling regimes governing the problem in nonlinear and adaptive network dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Adamatzky, Panagiotis Mougkogiannis

item.title: CoBe: A Benchmark For Conversational Counterfactual Text Editing
item.description: arXiv:2610.13057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Counterfactual text editing is the ability to revise a given text in light of a hypothetical change while preserving facts not causally affected by that change. When asked what would have happened if a doctor had not recommended surgery, the model output should retain the patient's medical history and modify only the consequences of the decision. This requires causal understanding: a model must determine, without being explicitly instructed to, what events are affected by the hypothetical change and what should remain fixed. This skill is central to human reasoning, especially in safety-critical domains like healthcare or law. By contrast, the task of associational text generation merely generates text statistically associated with the altered condition. In the medical example, an associational response might make the patient's symptoms less severe because milder cases correlate with no surgery. Such responses produce a plausible scenario, but not the counterfactual version of the given one. Prior counterfactual-text datasets do not clearly separate these modes of reasoning. We introduce the Counterfactual Benchmark (CoBe), a testbed for models' zero-shot ability to counterfactually edit a given textual scenario when prompted to do so in a conversationally natural way. CoBe contains 2000 questions spanning healthcare, science and engineering, business, and everyday scenarios. We test a suite of frontier and smaller models, with frontier systems achieving an average score of $58.05\%$. Our findings indicate that models frequently default to associational generation rather than preserving the causal structure of the original scenario. Moreover, performance does not scale consistently with either model size or output token length, suggesting that the failure may reflect model training objectives rather than insufficient model capacity.
item.dc:creator: Arvind Raghavan, Inwoo Hwang, Shreyas Havaldar, Kai-Zhan Lee, Aurghya Maiti, Yushu Pan, Jeffrey Wu, Mingxuan Li, Elias Bareinboim

item.title: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
item.description: arXiv:2610.13703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The fast pace in which protocols, frameworks, and technologies are being proposed for LLM-based agents results in a complex scenario for anyone aiming to create state-of-the-art AI solutions. Without an assessment on how different protocols, frameworks, and libraries work together to compose an Agentic Web solution, developers and organizations face different challenges (e.g., skilling, governance, infrastructure) even before becoming part of the Agentic Web ecosystem. In this context, we propose a system for performing Agentic Web evaluations called MASTIF (Multi-Agent System TestIng Framework) and present a baseline assessment of Agentic Web technologies, including 3 LLMs, 3 protocols, and 4 agent implementation frameworks, against 300 Mind2Web benchmark tasks. Results suggest that selecting a task-specific technology stack may result in gains of task completion rate, efficiency score, and social value stability scores; and reductions in verbosity and time to complete tasks. With the presented results, we expect to present a baseline in terms of metrics and results for this complex and fast evolving scenario for those aiming at designing, assessing, and developing multi-agent systems.
item.dc:creator: Vagner Figueredo de Santana, Diogo Cortiz

item.title: A Hardware-Native Trapped-Ion Hybrid Qudit-Oscillator Instruction Set
item.description: arXiv:2610.13843v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling trapped-ion processors by adding ions remains challenging. A complementary route exploits the multilevel internal structure of each ion to increase the computational Hilbert space per ion. We introduce a hardware-native hybrid qudit-oscillator instruction set for a general d-level internal register coupled to bosonic modes and prove that three of its native operation families suffice for universality of one qudit coupled to several modes. Adding an entangling operation between ions extends universality to a connected register of several qudits. The architecture natively supports both phase-space and sideband instruction sets and is implemented in the open-source framework HybridLane. As a representative application, we reproduce the dissipative vibronic dynamics of a three-chromophore complex previously simulated on a hybrid qubit-oscillator superconducting platform. Moving from a one-qubit-per-state register to a single qudit stores the entire electronic manifold in one ion, so every electronic coupling becomes a local intra-ion transition and the lab-frame Hamiltonian compiles directly into the ISA. Under the stated sequential timing model from a 40Ca+ qudit processor, one Trotter step is projected to run about ten times faster on the qudit, with an average RMSE of approximately 1.1 percent against the published reference.
item.dc:creator: Masoud Hakimi Heris, Yuan Liu, Frank Mueller

item.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.13918v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clinical sleep medicine repeatedly documents profound divergences between objective sleep duration and subjective daytime impairment, notably exemplified by sleep state misperception in paradoxical insomnia and boundary instability in narcolepsy type 1. Here, we present DyssomniaNN: a multi-scale biophysical computational framework coupling Borb\'ely's two-process regulation of sleep homeostasis and circadian drive with Saper's hypothalamic reciprocal flip-flop circuit and a recurrent corticothalamic leaky integrate-and-fire spiking neural network. We formalize five clinical cohorts across an identical 72-hour photoperiod: healthy control, circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder (delayed-phase), chronic insomnia, paradoxical insomnia, and narcolepsy type 1. The synthetic local field potential converges closely with empirical human electroencephalography spectra from the PhysioNet Sleep-EDF database across all canonical frequency bands (spectral mean absolute error of 0.33--0.35). Furthermore, we introduce the Well-Rested Index to quantify restorative efficacy. Simulations reveal that sleep duration fails to predict restorative recovery: paradoxical insomnia achieves normal total sleep time (21.15 h) yet yields low restoration (37.6%) from unsuppressed cortical beta-band intrusion, whereas hypocretin deficiency in narcolepsy produces severe nocturnal fragmentation (781 min of wake after sleep onset) and 35 sleep-onset rapid eye movement periods. DyssomniaNN provides an in silico platform for mechanistic sleep research and virtual neuropharmacology.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Szelogowski

item.title: Differentiable Partitioning With Dual-Max 3D Wirelength Model and Hybrid Bonding Terminal Awareness for Optimized 3D Placement
item.description: arXiv:2609.06408v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Research on 3D integrated circuits (3D-ICs) physical design has expanded rapidly in recent years, driven by the increasing adoption of hybrid bonding and the demand for higher integration density. Continued scaling of hybrid-bonding pitch supports higher vertical interconnect density and finer-grained circuit partitioning in 3D-ICs. Hybrid bonding-enabled 3D-ICs offer substantial benefits in interconnect scaling and system integration, yet tier assignment remains challenging because it jointly determines 3D wirelength and hybrid bonding terminal (HBT) assignment. This paper presents a differentiable partitioning framework that directly optimizes placement-aware tier assignment for 3D-ICs through gradient-based optimization. Discrete tier assignment is relaxed to continuous probabilities, and a Dual-Max 3D wirelength model is introduced as a placement-aware surrogate for tier-specific half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL). In addition, a terminal-aware cutsize penalty gives higher weights to cross-die nets with predicted HBT overlaps, and a local balance penalty discourages regional area overflow on each tier. On ten OpenROAD benchmarks, our method reduces final die-to-die (D2D) HPWL by 8.05% and 14.81% on average relative to hMETIS and TritonPart, respectively. On the seven benchmarks with available CoPlace results, the average HPWL reduction is 10.33%. The source code for the differentiable partitioner and the integrated 3D placement flow is publicly available to support reproducibility.
item.dc:creator: Liwen Jiang, Xu Shi, Rufeng Xiao, Changhao Yan, Rujun Jiang, Zhiang Wang, Keren Zhu

item.title: Classical and Quantum Heuristics for the Binary Paint Shop Problem
item.description: arXiv:2509.15294v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Binary Paint Shop Problem (BPSP) is an $\mathsf{APX}$-hard optimisation problem arising in automotive manufacturing: given a sequence of $2n$ cars, comprising $n$ distinct models each appearing twice, the task is to decide which of two colours to paint each car so that the two occurrences of each model are painted differently, while minimising consecutive colour swaps. Performance is measured by the paint swap ratio -- the average number of colour changes per car -- which directly affects production efficiency and cost. Prior work showed that the Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) at depth $p=7$ achieves a ratio of $0.393$, outperforming the then-best-known classical heuristic, Recursive Greedy, with a proven asymptotic expected ratio of $0.4$ [Phys. Rev. A 104, 012403 (2021)]. More recently, the Recursive Star Greedy (RSG) heuristic was proposed with a conjectured expected ratio of $0.361$. Here, we formally reduce BPSP to weighted MaxCut, yielding an exact Ising formulation, and benchmark two state-of-the-art low-depth QAOA variants -- eXpressive QAOA and Recursive QAOA -- at $p=1$ (denoted XQAOA$_1$ and RQAOA$_1$) against four classical BPSP heuristics. Across instances ranging from $2^7$ to $2^{12}$ cars, XQAOA$_1$ achieves an average paint-swap ratio of $0.357$; in our instance-wise benchmarks, it outperforms RQAOA$_1$ on almost all instances and each of the four classical baselines, including RSG, on every instance. Surprisingly, RQAOA$_1$ deteriorates with problem size despite employing provably near-optimal QAOA$_1$ parameters at each recursive step, eventually falling behind RSG at the largest sizes. To our knowledge, this is the first report of size-dependent performance degradation of RQAOA$_1$ at scale. In contrast, XQAOA$_1$ remains stable across all tested sizes, with no evidence of size-dependent degradation.
item.dc:creator: V Vijendran, Dax Enshan Koh, Ping Koy Lam, Syed M Assad

item.title: Breaking Memory Bottlenecks in Quantum Control Systems for More Precise Experiments and Higher Throughput Computing
item.description: arXiv:2608.06318v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As quantum computing matures, there is an increasing need for deeper and longer experiments to characterize quantum devices precisely and higher circuit throughput to validate more domain applications. However, this need is hindered by a memory bottleneck at the quantum control system layer, arising from the limited capacity of on-chip block random-access memory (BRAM) and the non-deterministic latency of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM). To break this bottleneck, we present Ant-Q, a memory hierarchy design for the QubiC 2.0 control system that integrates DRAM with BRAM to support pipelined quantum circuit execution while keeping inter-circuit timing deterministic whenever each circuit outlasts the refill of the next. A switch between command buffers then takes a constant 134 ns and, inside a circuit, acts on the qubit as a 144 ns idle. On the bench, Ant-Q runs deep one- and two-qubit randomized benchmarking beyond the command capacity of the baseline. For circuits with at least 1000 shots, it reduces the time the board spends beyond the circuit execution from 18.91%-104.54% to at most 0.53% of the execution time, and it improves the board-level throughput of 30-circuit batches by 51.06% against a baseline with the same shared tables (59.90% against the stock baseline). On a transmon qubit, Ant-Q executes a 5101-Clifford sequence and acquires uninterrupted 100 s Ramsey records with 0.01 Hz frequency spacing. In simulations, these records detect 1/f frequency noise of 1.37 and 1.62 times lower spectral density than the same records split into the 2.048 s runs of the baseline. The measured spectra resolve no 1/f component and match the measurement floor from 0.1 to 100 Hz. Ant-Q has been merged into the open-source QubiC gateware and software.
item.dc:creator: Yicheng Guang, Neel Vora, Yilun Xu, Yueqi Chen, Gang Huang

item.title: Claim-Gated Source-Risk Auditing for Generative Search
item.description: arXiv:2609.29145v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A generative search answer can cite a supported passage yet omit a source relationship that changes its interpretation. We specify a claim-gated audit of the query-source-answer tuple. An omission is resolved only when relationship evidence, answer adoption, materiality, and disclosure are all observed; incomplete evidence remains unresolved rather than being treated as independence. The specification separates this endpoint from citation support and review priority, and binds decisions to versioned evidence spans. A reference checker makes the record contract executable. On an exhaustive synthetic suite, it reproduces all 81 three-state predicate combinations and rejects 192 deliberately malformed records. Common-guard baselines and predicate ablations isolate endpoint logic from missing-evidence handling, while controlled transitions check support separation and evidence removal. These are finite contract-conformance results, not detector accuracy or evidence of improved user outcomes. We define the independent annotation, held-out evaluation, and paired utility tests still required to establish semantic validity and deployment benefit.
item.dc:creator: Kainan Zhou, Chuhong Xu, Gangzhen Qian, Zhaoyi Li

item.title: Energy-Aware Receiver-initiated MAC Protocol for Energy Harvesting IoT
item.description: arXiv:2610.11492v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Energy harvesting (EH) technology has emerged as a key approach for extending the operational autonomy of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. In this context, medium access control (MAC) protocols for EH-IoT make use of the harvested energy efficiently to enhance the application performance. However, many existing MAC protocols rely on stored energy the battery in devising energy-aware strategies, which can interrupt the device operation and hinder the execution of ongoing tasks in dynamic and low EH conditions. To address this, this paper presents an energy-aware receiver-initiated MAC protocol for EH-IoT devices, called EARI-MAC, that adjusts the duty cycle of the receiver device based on stored energy and current harvesting power using the mathematical formulation. This approach supports sustained receiver operation under low EH conditions and improved application performance when harvested energy is abundant. The performance of the EARI-MAC has been evaluated in simulation using the real solar data gathered in Novi Sad, for three consecutive days. The simulation results demonstrate that the EARI-MAC utilizes the available energy resources efficiently and improves the packet delivery ratio and network throughput by more than 10%, reduces the receiver energy consumption by 5.6% and 8.2% and energy consumption per bit by 9.6% and 13.9% compared with QPPD-MAC and energy-unaware MAC, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Sohail Sarang, Praveen Kumar Donta, Dejan Vukobratovi\'c
